# Font fidelity and performance in 0.3

CFF2 instances now retain the static CFF2 table emitted by HarfBuzz. FreeType receives the resolved Type 2 programs and private hint dictionaries directly. The previous outline-to-CFF1 reconstruction has been removed.

`SKTypeface.GetDocumentFontData()` supplies a separate static SFNT for document embedding. For CFF2, the converter preserves stem operators, hint masks, counter masks, and private hint dictionaries. It expands local/global subroutines, converts INDEX/container structures to CID-keyed CFF1, and splits long operand batches to respect the CFF1 stack limit. It preserves original glyph IDs and cubic control coordinates; it does not tessellate or reconstruct outlines. Native rendering and document embedding therefore use the format each consumer supports without discarding the original hint program.

The independent fixtures in `tests/fixtures/create-hint-fixtures.py` author explicit stem/mask instructions and generate reference instances using Python fontTools. Tests compare pixels from the JS-created and independently generated native CFF2 and CFF1 instances at weights 100, 500, and 900, at sizes 7, 9, 11, 13, 18, 32, and 60. Separate fixtures exercise local/global subroutines, binary mask bytes, and operand batches longer than 48 values. All comparisons pass byte-for-byte using aliased, fully hinted FreeType rendering. A separate negative-control fixture strips the hint programs; its native pixels differ, confirming that these tests detect the original fidelity loss.

`fonts-native.test.mjs` compares every metric field, glyph IDs, advances, and glyph bounds with independently executed .NET SkiaSharp for the exact bundled DejaVuSans font. Font identity is recorded by SHA-256. The new native extension supplies `ForceAutoHinting`, `BaselineSnap`, complete `SKFontMetrics`, native glyph paths, empty typefaces, and a registered-font provider whose native fallback resolves missing glyphs during paragraph shaping. No operating-system fonts are assumed to be accessible to a web page.

The public API adds canonical `SKFontVariationAxis`, `SKFontVariationPositionCoordinate`, `SKFontPaletteOverride`, `SKFontMetrics`, variation count/properties/destination spans, `Clone` coordinate/palette overloads, and `SKFontArguments.PaletteIndex` / `PaletteOverrides`. `VariationDesignPosition` accepts direct array assignment and remains iterable. Font-manager matching indexes families and caches CSS style/character matches. Registered BCP47 language preferences may be supplied as `RegisterFont(data, family, { Languages: ['pl'] })`; later BCP47 entries have higher preference, matching Skia's ordering convention. Browser font discovery remains scoped to registered or explicitly imported fonts.

`SKFontCache` controls a 32 MiB default budget shared by parsed-source bytes, resolved instances, and owned native typeface references. Hash matches are verified against every source byte. Returned typefaces own independent native references; eviction and `Clear()` release cache references without invalidating callers. Palette and normalized-axis keys distinguish variants. The byte budget estimates retained font data and excludes JavaScript object and native allocator overhead.

The checked benchmark `FONT-PERFORMANCE.json` measures repeated Roboto Flex weight-750 instancing. Median cold construction was 3.30 ms and cached construction was 0.0113 ms (about 293× for this repeated-axes workload); a retained clone was 0.0051 ms. These are shared-host Node/WASM observations, not universal browser throughput claims. `scripts/benchmark-fonts.mjs` reproduces the workload. Interactive changes to previously unseen coordinates still require instancing work.

CFF1 has format limits independent of the renderer: the converter rejects more than 256 distinct font dictionaries and malformed or unresolved programs rather than discarding hint data. Native CFF2 rendering remains available for those font formats. This focused differential set is evidence for the tested behavior, not an exhaustive corpus of every font ever produced.
